Definition: altitude, i.e. concretely (an elevated place), abstractly (elevation, figuratively (elation), or adverbially (aloft)
BiblicalUsage: mârôwm is height, an elevated place and the idea of being lifted up. In 2 Kings 19:22 Sennacherib lifts his eyes on high against the Holy One of Israel, and in 2 Kings 19:23 he boasts of coming up to the height of the mountains. In 2 Samuel 22:17 God sends from above and draws David out of many waters, and in Ecclesiastes 10:6 folly is set in great dignity while the rich sit low. The word is the high place, God's or man's.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mârôwm teaches me to lift my eyes to the God on high. I hold that the high places of men are nothing beside Him.
RelatedTopics: God's Sovereignty; Majesty of God; Pride
